read.sections.0.text.note: "wheat and rice" is ข้าวสาลีและข้าว; Tigris and Euphrates are แม่น้ำไทกริส and แม่น้ำยูเฟรทีส, as in Lesson 7's picture.
read.sections.0.text.source: Every community needs water to drink, cook and wash. In many places, a river gives fresh water all year. Farmers dig small canals to carry river water to their fields. When a river floods, it leaves a layer of mud on the land, and this mud makes the soil fertile, so crops like wheat and rice grow well. Rivers also give people fish to eat. That is why some of the first large settlements grew beside rivers. In ancient Egypt, people farmed along the Nile, and in today's Iraq, people farmed between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers. The River site in Riverlands has the same kind of flat, fertile land.
read.sections.0.text.back: Every community needs water for drinking, cooking and washing. In many places a river gives fresh water all year. Farmers dig small canals to bring water from the river to the fields. When a river floods, it leaves a layer of mud on the land. This mud makes the soil fertile, so crops such as wheat and rice grow well. Rivers also give fish for food. That is why some of the first big settlements grew up beside rivers. In ancient Egypt people farmed beside the Nile, and in what is now Iraq people farmed between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers. The river site in Riverlands has the same kind of fertile flat land.

read.sections.0.simpler.source: People need water to drink, cook and wash. A river gives water. Farmers take river water to their fields. Sometimes a river floods. Then it leaves mud on the land. The mud makes the soil fertile. Crops grow well there. People also catch fish in rivers. So many early settlements grew next to rivers. One example is Egypt, by the Nile River. The River site on the map has fertile land too.
read.sections.0.simpler.back: People need water to drink, cook and wash. Rivers give water. Farmers bring water from the river to the fields. Sometimes the river floods and leaves mud on the land. The mud makes the soil fertile, so crops grow well. People can also catch fish in the river. So many early settlements were beside rivers. One example is Egypt, beside the Nile. The river site on the map has fertile soil too.

read.sections.1.heading.source: Rivers help people travel and trade
read.sections.1.heading.back: Rivers help people travel and trade

read.sections.1.text.note: Bangkok and the Chao Phraya are in the English; KEY_TERMS gives กรุงเทพฯ and แม่น้ำเจ้าพระยา (the checker warns that "Phraya" does not appear: on purpose). Kinshasa is กินชาซา, the Congo River แม่น้ำคองโก. "up and down the river" is ทั้งต้นน้ำและปลายน้ำ.
read.sections.1.text.source: Rivers can work like roads made of water. Long ago, before there were trucks or trains, boats could carry heavy goods, like grain, wood and cloth, more easily than people or animals could. Towns often grew at places where boats stopped so that people could buy and sell. Many important cities today still sit on rivers. Bangkok in Thailand is on the Chao Phraya River, and Kinshasa, a large city in Central Africa, is on the Congo River. In Riverlands, boats can stop at the River site. A town there could trade with other towns up and down the river.
read.sections.1.text.back: A river can work like a road made of water. Long ago, before trucks or trains, boats could carry heavy goods such as grain, wood and cloth more easily than people or animals. Towns often grew where boats stopped, so people could buy and sell. Many important cities today still stand beside rivers. Bangkok in Thailand is on the Chao Phraya River, and Kinshasa, a big city in Central Africa, is on the Congo River. In Riverlands, boats can stop at the river site, so a town there could trade with other towns upstream and downstream.

So towns grew where boats stopped. Many big cities are still on rivers. Bangkok is on a river in Thailand. Kinshasa is on the Congo River in Africa. On the map, boats can stop at the River site.
read.sections.1.simpler.back: Boats can travel on rivers. Long ago there were no trucks or trains. Boats carried heavy goods like rice and wood. People bought and sold these goods in towns. So towns grew where boats stopped. Many big cities are still beside rivers. Bangkok is beside a river in Thailand. Kinshasa is beside the Congo River in Africa. read.sections.2.text.note: Floods are a sensitive subject for some learners (see sensitiveNotes). "high banks of earth" is คันดินสูง in the standard text, กำแพงดินสูง in the simpler one.
read.sections.2.text.source: Living near a river has risks too. After heavy rain, a river can flood, and water covers roads, fields and homes for a time. People who live by rivers have found ways to prepare. In parts of Cambodia and Brazil, some families build houses on tall wooden legs, so water can pass underneath. In other places, people build high banks of earth along the river to keep the water out. Some towns are built on higher ground, like the Hill site, but then people must carry water further. No place is perfect, so a good choice compares the benefits with the risks.
read.sections.2.text.back: Living near a river has risks too. After heavy rain a river can overflow and flood. The flood covers roads, fields and homes for a while. People who live by rivers find ways to prepare. In parts of Cambodia and Brazil, some families build houses on tall wooden posts so water can flow under the house. In other places people build high earth banks along the river to hold back the water. Some towns are built on high ground, like the hill site, but then people must carry water further. No place is perfect, so a good choice means comparing benefits with risks.

read.sections.2.simpler.source: Rivers can bring problems too. After a lot of rain, a river can flood. Water covers fields, roads and homes for a time. People find ways to get ready. Some families build houses on tall legs. Then water can go under the house. Some towns build high walls of earth by the river. Other towns are on a hill. But then people carry water a long way. Every place has good things and risks.
read.sections.2.simpler.back: Rivers can bring problems too. After a lot of rain, there can be a flood. The flood covers fields, roads and houses for a while. People find ways to prepare. Some families build houses on tall posts, so water flows under the house. Some towns build tall earth walls along the river. Some towns are on hills, but people must carry water far. Every place has both good points and risks.

watch.summary.note: King Hammurabi is กษัตริย์ฮัมมูราบี, as in Lesson 7 (the checker warns that the Latin name does not appear: on purpose). ziggurats: ซิกกูรัต. "his laws" is กฎหมายของพระองค์ (a plain royal pronoun); check against the KEY_TERMS rule of plain words for kings.
watch.summary.source: This video is about Mesopotamia. The name means 'land between rivers'. It was a flat, fertile area between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers. Today this land is in Iraq, Syria and Kuwait. The good soil was great for farming, so people farmed there for thousands of years. About 5,000 to 6,000 years ago, some farming villages grew into some of the world's first cities. People in these cities built large temples called ziggurats. They counted in groups of 60. That is why an hour has 60 minutes. They also made one of the first kinds of writing. They pressed marks into wet clay. A king named Hammurabi had his laws written down. Many of these ideas are still used today.
watch.summary.back: This video is about Mesopotamia. The name means "the land between rivers". Mesopotamia is a fertile plain between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers. Today this land is in Iraq, Syria and Kuwait. The good soil was very good for farming, so people farmed there for thousands of years. About 5,000 to 6,000 years ago some farming villages grew into some of the world's first cities. People in these cities built huge temples called ziggurats. They counted in groups of 60. That is why 1 hour has 60 minutes. They also invented one of the first kinds of writing, by pressing marks into wet clay. A king named Hammurabi had his laws written down. Many of these ideas are still used today.
